title: Solitary Island of the Princess and the Dragon King's Palace
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Heiji Hattori, Kazuha Toyama, Ran, Kogoro Mouri) omitted by convention, even though Heiji drives the decoy trick that exposes the culprit -- that trick is represented via Daito's attempted attack on the intended real target (Kume) rather than on Heiji. Episode 0292 subtitles are not available locally, so the middle stretch (captain Shimoji's murder itself, most suspect interrogations) is reconstructed only from what 0291 and 0293 state or reference about it; Shimoji's cause of death ('bludgeoned near a crashed boat') is carried over from the old case file and flagged uncertain since it could not be independently verified against a transcript. Corrections vs. the old lower-fidelity case file: (1) the old file's culprit call (Mikihiko Daito) IS correct here, unlike some other rebuilds; (2) the old file's clue c1 conflates two separate messages into one -- the permanent pillar carving inside the cottage (left a year earlier by a stranded, now-dead gang member, and never tide-exposed at all) versus the temporary message Daito wrote in the sand next to Taira's body, whose false urgency came from the tour cruiser's wake soaking the sand past the true high-water line, not from the tide itself -- these are now two distinct object nodes; (3) the old file's has_motive_against edge mischaracterizes Daito's motive as 'financial', when the transcript makes clear it is revenge -- Daito is the mayor's former butler whose fiancee, housekeeper Yoshiko Matsumoto, was killed by the gang during the original robbery, and the 'financial' angle (the stolen 200-million-yen folding screen, code-named 'the princess') is the gang's motive from four years earlier, not Daito's; (4) the old file omits the entire backstory network needed to make sense of the case -- Matsumoto, mayor Kaneshiro, the stranded dead gang member, and the reveal that victim Yoshie Taira was secretly Kaneshiro's estranged stepdaughter Miyako who staged her own kidnapping five years earlier and was herself a gang member. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Wet sand around the sand message looked exactly like a high-tide line, but it actually came from the cruiser's wake, not the tide -- once that's separated out, the message could only have been written at high tide, not the low tide everyone assumed, which reopens who had opportunity.

Daito attacked a decoy dressed and positioned as Kume, believing it was really Kume he was killing -- proving he already knew where and who his next target was, something only the real killer could know.
Daito casually remarked 'I feel like Urashima Taro' near the spot where the screen had been sunk -- a reference only someone who knew the screen ('the princess') had been sunk there would make.
